description:
GRANTS NOTHING, ON PURPOSE. Empty `permissions` is the content of this file, not an unfinished edit.

WHY IT EXISTS. This is the capability set a browsing surface would be attached to if one ever lands. It is a pre-built boundary, not a boundary currently holding anything back: this build has no embedded webview at all (Tauri 2.12.5 gates `Window::add_child` and `WebviewBuilder` behind its `unstable` feature, which `Cargo.toml` does not enable, and exposes no history navigation on `Webview`), so there is no remote content in the app today. See the module header of `src/browser.rs`, which records the same three findings against the vendored crate source. The point of writing the empty set down now is that a future surface arrives with no route to IPC by default, and widening it becomes a visible diff in this file rather than an unnoticed inheritance.

WHAT THE EMPTY SET PROTECTS. Tauri grants a webview exactly the union of the capabilities whose `windows`/`webviews` patterns match its label, and nothing else. With no permissions here, a matching surface can reach no command: not `core:default` (so no app, window, event, path or resources commands and no Tauri API injection it could call), not `opener:default`, and none of this app's own commands - so no project file access, no agent credentials from the keychain, no PTY session or shell command, and no device or connection control. That is the same list `DENIED_TO_REMOTE_CONTENT` in `src/browser.rs` publishes, expressed here as configuration instead of prose.

NO `remote` KEY, DELIBERATELY. `remote` is what opts a capability's permissions in for non-local (http/https) origins. Its absence is load-bearing: even if a permission were added here by mistake, a remote page loaded into a matching surface would still not receive it. Do not add a `remote` block to this file.

THE LABEL CONSTRAINT - READ BEFORE CREATING ANY SURFACE. `capabilities/default.json` matches `"windows": ["main"]`, and per the Tauri capability contract a window pattern enables that capability on EVERY webview of the matching window, whatever the webview's own label. A browsing surface created as a child webview of the `main` window would therefore inherit `core:default` and `opener:default` from that file, and nothing in this capability can subtract them. A surface must be created in its own window whose label matches `browser-*`, never as a child of `main`.

CSP. Unrelated to this file and not to be solved here: a child webview is its own security origin and does not inherit the app document's Content-Security-Policy, so the app policy in `tauri.conf.json` is set to its strictest workable form with no carve-out for a browsing surface - no `frame-src` allowance, no widened `default-src`. Remote pages are never framed into the app document.
